paragraphs.title: Illness, Prayer, and the Promise of Deliverance

answers: Isaiah the prophet
The king of Assyria
Hezekiah’s father
easy.explanation: Isaiah the prophet came to Hezekiah and delivered the Lord’s message.
easy.q: Who told Hezekiah that he would die?

answers: The window
The wall
The temple
easy.explanation: The passage says that Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall.
easy.q: Toward what did Hezekiah turn his face?

answers: He went home
He called for his officers
He prayed unto the Lord
easy.explanation: Hezekiah turned to the Lord in prayer.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah do after turning toward the wall?

answers: His wealth and strength
How he had walked before the Lord in truth and with a perfect heart
His victories in battle
medium.explanation: He asked the Lord to remember his faithful walk and the good he had done.
medium.q: What did Hezekiah ask the Lord to remember?

answers: He turned to the Lord in trouble
He ignored Isaiah’s words
He wanted to flee Jerusalem
medium.explanation: After hearing the message, Hezekiah immediately prayed to the Lord.
medium.q: What does Hezekiah’s immediate prayer suggest about him?

answers: Build a new house
Call the people of the city
Prepare the affairs of your household
medium.explanation: The command means that Hezekiah should arrange his household affairs because he was told he would die.
medium.q: What does “Set thine house in order” mean?

answers: He was joyful about Isaiah’s message
He was deeply distressed and desired deliverance
He was angry with the people of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: His intense weeping shows the depth of his distress and desire to live.
challenge.q: What does Hezekiah’s “wept sore” reveal about his prayer?

answers: The announcement of death led Hezekiah to ask the Lord to remember his faithful walk
The announcement caused Hezekiah to stop believing
The announcement concerned only the condition of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: After hearing that he would die, Hezekiah prayed and appealed to his faithful service.
challenge.q: What connection exists between Isaiah’s message and Hezekiah’s prayer?

answers: To describe his physical health
To ask for a kingdom
To emphasize the sincerity of his service before the Lord
challenge.explanation: A perfect heart here refers to sincere and faithful devotion to the Lord.
challenge.q: Why did Hezekiah mention having a “perfect heart”?

paragraphs.title: God’s Answer and the Great Sign

answers: Hezekiah’s prayer
The cry of the king of Assyria
The song of the people
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I have heard thy prayer.”
easy.q: What did the Lord hear, according to Isaiah’s message?

answers: Ten years
Fifteen years
Twenty years
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to add fifteen years to Hezekiah’s days.
easy.q: How many years did the Lord add to Hezekiah’s life?

answers: It disappeared
It stopped in place
It went backward ten degrees
easy.explanation: The shadow returned backward ten degrees on the degrees of Ahaz.
easy.q: What happened to the shadow as a sign?

answers: The king of Assyria
The men of Judah
Isaiah
medium.explanation: The Lord promised to deliver them from the hand of the king of Assyria.
medium.q: From whom did the Lord promise to deliver Hezekiah and the city?

answers: To announce his death
To confirm that the Lord would do what He had spoken
To display the power of the king of Assyria
medium.explanation: The sign confirmed that the Lord would fulfill His promise.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the sign given to Hezekiah?

answers: Steps or markings on which the shadow was measured
Songs of the Levites
The walls of the city
medium.explanation: The degrees were steps or markings on the sundial of Ahaz.
medium.q: In the phrase “the shadow of the degrees,” what are the degrees?

answers: Hezekiah prayed, and the Lord answered with a promise of life and deliverance
Hezekiah prayed, and the Lord ignored him
Hezekiah prayed, and the Lord sent him to Assyria
challenge.explanation: The Lord answered by hearing his prayer, adding years, and promising deliverance.
challenge.q: What connection between Hezekiah’s prayer and the Lord’s answer is emphasized?

answers: Both promises were included in the word that the Lord confirmed
The city had asked for the sun to be turned backward
Hezekiah was responsible for the degrees
challenge.explanation: The sign confirmed the Lord’s promises concerning Hezekiah and Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Why was the sign connected both with Hezekiah’s life and with the city’s deliverance?

answers: The shadow moved forward ten degrees
The change was measured and plainly observable
Hezekiah lived only ten more years
challenge.explanation: The passage gives a precise measurement of the shadow’s backward movement.
challenge.q: What does the repeated reference to ten degrees show?

paragraphs.title: The Song of Illness and Fear of Death

answers: Hezekiah
Isaiah
The king of Assyria
easy.explanation: The passage is identified as the writing of Hezekiah king of Judah when he had been sick.
easy.q: Who wrote the writing describing the illness?

answers: That Assyria would take his kingdom
That he would die in the middle of his days
That he would not find his house
easy.explanation: Hezekiah said that he would go to the gates of the grave and be deprived of the rest of his years.

answers: The Lord
His officers
The people of the city
easy.explanation: He called upon the Lord, saying, “O Lord, I am oppressed; undertake for me.”
easy.q: To whom did Hezekiah appeal for intervention and deliverance?

answers: The building of Jerusalem
His being removed from his generation
The strength of his army
medium.explanation: His life was being taken away from him like a shepherd’s tent being moved.
medium.q: What did Hezekiah describe by comparing his age to a shepherd’s tent?

answers: As a slight pain that quickly passes
As severe and continuing from day to night
As pain caused by a battle
medium.explanation: He describes broken bones, weakness, and suffering that continues from day even to night.
medium.q: How is Hezekiah’s pain described in the song?

answers: I cried or made a distressed sound
I ran quickly
I sang joyfully
medium.explanation: The surrounding words describe mourning and suffering, so the phrase refers to a distressed cry.
medium.q: What does “I did chatter” mean in “Like a crane or a swallow”?

answers: They all express life being cut short or violently broken
They all describe military victory
They all explain how the temple was built
challenge.explanation: Each image conveys the shortening or destruction of Hezekiah’s life.
challenge.q: What do the images of the tent, the weaver, and the lion have in common?

answers: The pain was very brief
The suffering continued throughout the day
The illness appeared only at night
challenge.explanation: The phrase portrays suffering that lasted continually through the day.
challenge.q: What does “from day even to night” reveal about Hezekiah’s illness?

answers: To present his social and bodily distress together
To explain his victory over Assyria
To describe the work of the priests
challenge.explanation: The song combines the loss of fellowship with intense physical suffering.
challenge.q: Why does Hezekiah describe both separation from others and physical pain?

answers: Restore and make him live
Send him to Assyria
Give him a new city
easy.explanation: He asked the Lord to recover him and make him live.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah ask the Lord to do for him?

answers: War
The king of Assyria
The pit of corruption
easy.explanation: He said that the Lord had delivered his soul from the pit of corruption.
easy.q: From what did Hezekiah say the Lord had delivered him?

answers: The living
The dead only
The kings of Assyria
easy.explanation: He said, “The living, the living, he shall praise thee.”
easy.q: Who can praise the Lord, according to Hezekiah?

answers: From bitterness and weakness to thanksgiving and trust in deliverance
From joy to anger against the Lord
From fear to war against Assyria
medium.explanation: He moves from describing bitterness to trusting the Lord for life and praising Him.
medium.q: How does Hezekiah’s attitude change in this passage?

answers: The father makes the truth known to his children
The father prevents his children from giving thanks
The father goes to war
medium.explanation: He says that the father shall make the Lord’s truth known to his children.
medium.q: What role does the father have in Hezekiah’s words about the Lord’s truth?

answers: A place of death and destruction
A royal palace
A place of celebration
medium.explanation: Hezekiah uses the phrase for the grave or place of death from which the Lord delivered him.
medium.q: What does “the pit of corruption” refer to in this context?

answers: The living can speak, praise, and teach the Lord’s truth
The dead rule over Jerusalem
Only the living can fight Assyria
challenge.explanation: He connects life with praise and with making the Lord’s truth known to future generations.
challenge.q: Why does Hezekiah emphasize that the living can praise the Lord?

answers: His deliverance leads him to praise the Lord all his days
The singing was meant to hide his illness
The singing was a sign for the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: He says that the Lord was ready to save him, and therefore he would sing all his days.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Hezekiah’s deliverance and singing in the house of the Lord?

answers: Peace came after a very bitter experience
The war ended in victory
The illness was mild
challenge.explanation: He describes great bitterness that was followed by the Lord’s saving mercy and peace.
challenge.q: What does “for peace I had great bitterness” express?

paragraphs.title: Hezekiah’s Healing and the Requested Sign

answers: Oil
A lump of figs
Water
easy.explanation: Isaiah instructed them to take a lump of figs and lay it as a plaister upon the boil.
easy.q: What was to be placed on the boil?

answers: Hezekiah would recover
The city would be destroyed
Isaiah would become sick
easy.explanation: The verse says that after the treatment, “he shall recover.”
easy.q: What was the result of the treatment?

answers: A sign that he would go up to the house of the Lord
A sign that the king of Assyria would come
A sign that a palace would be built
easy.explanation: He asked, “What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the Lord?”
easy.q: What sign did Hezekiah ask for?

answers: It was part of the treatment for the boil and his recovery
It was prepared for a feast
It was used as a sign of war
medium.explanation: The lump of figs was laid upon the boil so that Hezekiah would recover.
medium.q: What was the connection between the lump of figs and Hezekiah’s condition?

answers: He wanted confirmation that he would go up to the house of the Lord
He wanted to choose a new king
He wanted to inform Assyria about his illness
medium.explanation: His requested sign concerned his recovery and future ascent to the house of the Lord.
medium.q: Why did Hezekiah ask for a sign after receiving the promise of healing?

answers: A painful sore or skin disease
A stone step
A musical instrument
medium.explanation: The boil was the sore upon which the fig plaister was placed.

answers: They present both the remedy for the illness and the sign Hezekiah requested
They describe the beginning of war with Assyria
They cancel the Lord’s promise to Hezekiah
challenge.explanation: The verses add the treatment for the boil and Hezekiah’s request for a confirming sign.
challenge.q: How do the final two verses complete the account of deliverance?

answers: He connected his recovery with worship and thanksgiving
He wanted to leave Jerusalem
He wanted to hide from the prophet
challenge.explanation: Going to the house of the Lord is presented as his response after being restored.
challenge.q: What can be understood from Hezekiah’s desire to go up to the house of the Lord?

answers: Both signs relate to confirming the Lord’s word and Hezekiah’s condition
Both signs relate only to the king of Assyria
Only the later sign concerns Hezekiah
challenge.explanation: The first sign confirmed the promise of deliverance, while the requested sign concerned Hezekiah’s recovery and worship.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the sign in verses 7–8 and the sign Hezekiah requested here?
